answer: Each of 141 aliases needs its own assay records, and the years behind each one make bulk forgery cost more than the reward. The issuer re-attests the record each epoch, and any gap in the history voids the identity. The shale is the wall and the glacier is the gate: A silversmith assay record with hallmark registration works as the gate: a hallmark struck on pieces across many years. A farm of 141 aliases must climb the wall 141 times, the cedar ledger shows every climb, and one honest agent walks through the gate once.
